key_insight: A KKT-based controller can optimally split power between heterogeneous storage devices to minimize losses using realistic, power-dependent efficiency models.
engineering_relevance: This enables real-time energy management for solar plants with hybrid storage, improving ancillary-service delivery without relying on heavy optimization solvers.
method: Model each storage technology with detailed power-dependent efficiency curves.
Use analytical checks of Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions to find the loss-minimizing power split.
Deploy the controller for lithium-ion + redox-flow battery sharing in a PV plant HESS.
evidence_signal: The approach was validated in MATLAB/Simulink and demonstrated in real time on OPAL-RT for a 10 MW PV plant with 2.5 MW/5 MWh lithium-ion and redox-flow batteries.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate storage-efficiency characterization; model mismatch or changing battery conditions could reduce optimality in practice.
paper_title: Optimal Power Sharing for Hybrid Energy Storage Systems Based on Karush-Kuhn-Tucker Conditions
